title: Course Schedule
source: canonical Course Schedule concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: There are num_courses courses, numbered 0 to num_courses - 1, and a list of prerequisite pairs, where each pair [course, prereq] means prereq must be taken before course. Return True when every course can be finished in some order, False when a circular dependency makes that impossible.

examples.explanation: Each course waits for the other; neither can ever start.

hints: Courses with no prerequisites can always be taken; taking them removes them as prerequisites for others.
Repeatedly take a course whose remaining prerequisite count is zero, and subtract it from the counts of courses it unlocks.
If the count of taken courses never reaches num_courses, a circular dependency swallowed the rest.
solution: Kahn topological sort: count incoming prerequisites, repeatedly take a course whose count reached zero, and decrement the courses it unlocks. All courses taken means no cycle. O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include no prerequisites, a direct loop, and a self-dependency

visible.failNote: a chain of prerequisites is always schedulable
a two-course loop can never start
